title: Probability of a genuine intersection at the special coordinate
statement: Fix an integer $n \ge 1$, and let the sample space consist of all tuples $(T, x_T, y_T, c)$, where $T \in \{1,\dots,n\}$ is a distinguished coordinate, $x_T, y_T \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ are two Boolean values, and $c$ assigns to each coordinate one of the three labels *neither*, *leftOnly*, or *rightOnly*; equip this finite space with the uniform probability measure. Then the event that the distinguished coordinate is a genuine intersection, namely $\{x_T = \mathrm{true} \text{ and } y_T = \mathrm{true}\}$, has probability $\tfrac14$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number (n ≥ 1)
finite sample space of tuples (T, x_T, y_T, c) with the uniform probability measure
event that x_T = true and y_T = true
replaced: The hard distribution creates an intersection with probability $1 / 4$.
